nodes.label: DEBATE Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Large-scale empirical benchmark for evaluating authenticity of multi-agent role-playing LLM interactions; 29,417 messages from 2,792 participants

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Opinion Dynamics
nodes.rationale: Evaluates authenticity of group dynamics in role-playing LLM agents; addresses premature consensus convergence and unnatural alignment patterns

nodes.label: DEBATE Benchmark Dataset
nodes.rationale: Large-scale empirical benchmark for evaluating multi-agent role-playing LLM systems, capturing opinion trajectories from 2,792 U.S. participants across multi-round, multi-party interactions with 29,417 messages.

nodes.label: Depth Topics (TDepth)
nodes.rationale: Seven topics with known scientific consensus or ground truth, selected to elicit diverse opinions and study opinion dynamics with high-entropy topics.

nodes.label: Breadth Topics (TBreadth)
nodes.rationale: 100 topics from World Values Survey and Pew Global Attitudes Survey, selected for highest response entropy to reflect public disagreement without ground truth.

nodes.label: LLM Role-play Agent Construction
nodes.rationale: Digital twin agents conditioned on memory modules reflecting human participants' first-person perspective, including demographics, initial opinions, tweets, and conversation history.

nodes.label: Simulation Mode 1: Next Message Prediction
nodes.rationale: Predicts immediate response in real conversations using human tweets, human prior utterances, and human current round context.

nodes.label: Simulation Mode 2: Tweet-guided Conversation Simulation
nodes.rationale: Simulates private conversations given trace of real public tweets, using human tweets but simulated prior and current utterances.

nodes.label: Simulation Mode 3: Full Conversation Simulation
nodes.rationale: Simulates agents' dynamics from initial conditions using initial human tweet plus simulated subsequent tweets and utterances; classic opinion dynamics setup.

nodes.label: Utterance-level Evaluation Metrics
nodes.rationale: Semantic similarity, stance difference, length metrics, ROUGE-L, and on-topic utterance rate to assess alignment between LLM-generated and human utterances.

nodes.label: GPT-4o-mini-2024-07-18
nodes.rationale: Best-performing LLM in DEBATE evaluation, achieving strongest alignment on semantic similarity, ROUGE-L, and stance difference across all simulation modes.

nodes.label: Opinion Convergence in LLM Groups
nodes.rationale: LLM groups exhibit stronger opinion convergence in both public tweet stance and private self-reported opinion compared to human groups, with systematic individual shifts.

nodes.label: Positive Drift in Public Tweet Stance
nodes.rationale: LLM groups show significant increase in average tweet stance from round 1 to round 3, endorsing false statements in Depth topics, while human groups show no significant change.

nodes.label: Regression to the Mean Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Individuals with extreme initial stances tend to move toward midpoint; LLM agents show stronger correlations than humans in this tendency.

nodes.label: Partner Influence Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Individuals shift toward first partner's stance; LLM agents show greater susceptibility to partner influence than humans.

nodes.label: Memory Module Ablation Study
nodes.rationale: Systematic removal of memory components (prior chats, initial opinion, demographics, private profile) shows minimal impact in Mode 1 but degraded performance in Modes 2-3 when conversation history is simulated.

nodes.label: Supervised Fine-Tuning Limitations
nodes.rationale: SFT improves surface-level alignment (message length, ROUGE-L) but fails to enhance semantic similarity or stance alignment; suggests naive SFT encourages surface-form mimicry without behavioral alignment.

nodes.label: Human Data Collection Protocol
nodes.rationale: 2,792 U.S. participants recruited via Prolific, randomly assigned to 797 four-person groups, engaged in multi-round discussions with initial tweets, dyadic conversations, and final opinions.

nodes.label: On-Topic Utterance Classification
nodes.rationale: GPT-4o-mini classifier identifies utterances directly addressing discussion topic; validated against 200 human-labeled utterances with 90% accuracy; excludes conversational fillers and unrelated remarks.

nodes.label: Stance Score Classification
nodes.rationale: Maps utterances to six-point Likert scale stance scores [-2.5 to +2.5]; GPT-4o-mini classifier validated against 200 human-labeled utterances with 90% accuracy.

nodes.label: Semantic Similarity Metric (Ssem)
nodes.rationale: Cosine similarity between sentence embeddings; measures meaning-level alignment between LLM-generated and human utterances.

nodes.label: Stance Difference Metric (Δstance)
nodes.rationale: Absolute difference between stance scores; captures alignment in opinion polarity between LLM and human utterances.

nodes.label: Llama Model Variants
nodes.rationale: Llama-3.1-Tulu-3-8B-SFT, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct evaluated; represent pre- vs. post-RLHF checkpoints and varying model scales.

nodes.label: World Values Survey (WVS) Topics
nodes.rationale: Source for Breadth topics; 100 U.S.-administered questions selected for highest response entropy to reflect public disagreement.

nodes.label: Pew Global Attitudes Survey (PGAS) Topics
nodes.rationale: Source for Breadth topics; complements WVS with diverse policy and social value questions.

nodes.label: Round-wise Aggregated Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Each simulated utterance compared to all on-topic human utterances from same round and speaker; metrics averaged across utterances, agents, and rounds.

nodes.label: Jina Embeddings v3 Encoder
nodes.rationale: 1024-dimensional sentence encoder used for semantic similarity computation in evaluation metrics.

nodes.label: DEBATE Participant Demographics
nodes.rationale: 2,792 U.S. participants spanning ages 18-83 (M=39.5), 50.2% male, diverse ethnicities, education levels, income brackets, occupations, political identities, and religious affiliations.

nodes.label: DEBATE Message Count
nodes.rationale: 29,417 total messages across dataset; Depth subset 501 participants, Breadth subset 2,291 participants.

nodes.label: DEBATE Group Count
nodes.rationale: 797 four-person groups total; Depth subset 26.43 groups per topic average, Breadth subset 6.12 groups per topic average.
